# Load Necessary Packages

```{r}
library(dplyr)

```

# Read in Trumps tweet data and polling data and extracting what I need
```{r}
TrumpTweetsFull <- read.csv("C:/Users/Etienne Arnoult/Downloads/trump_presidency_tweets_2017_2020.csv")
TrumpTweetsRaw <- TrumpTweetsFull %>%
  select(date, lower_text, is_rt) # dataset has text already put into lowercase

PollsFull <- read.csv("C:/Users/Etienne Arnoult/Downloads/historical_net_approval_rate_first_term.csv")
```

# Trump Tweet Cleaning Genie
```{r}
TrumpTweetyCleanyGenie <- function(df) {
  
  # 1. Filter out retweets
  df <- df %>% filter(is_rt != "YES")
  
  # 2. Split into words
  df$lower_text <- strsplit(df$lower_text, "\\s+")
  
  # 3. Unnest to one word per row (date stays aligned)
  df <- df %>% unnest(lower_text)
  
  # 4. Remove @mentions, hashtags, and t.co links
  df <- df[!grepl("@", df$lower_text, fixed = TRUE), ]
  df <- df[!grepl("#", df$lower_text, fixed = TRUE), ]
  df <- df[!grepl("t.co", df$lower_text, fixed = TRUE), ]
  
  # 5. Load stopword + replacement lists and capture object names
  stops_obj <- load(url("https://github.com/Reilly-ConceptsCognitionLab/reillylab_publicdata/blob/main/Temple_stops25.rda?raw=true"))
  repl_obj  <- load(url("https://github.com/Reilly-ConceptsCognitionLab/reillylab_publicdata/blob/main/replacements_25.rda?raw=true"))
  
  Temple_stops25     <- get(stops_obj[1])
  replacement_lookup <- get(repl_obj[1])
  
  # 6. Apply contraction replacement BEFORE removing punctuation
  df$lower_text[df$lower_text %in% names(replacement_lookup)] <- 
    replacement_lookup[df$lower_text[df$lower_text %in% names(replacement_lookup)]]
  
  # 7. NOW remove digits and punctuation
  df$lower_text <- gsub("\\d", " ", df$lower_text)
  df$lower_text <- gsub("[^A-Za-z ]", " ", df$lower_text)
  
  # 8. Trim whitespace created by cleaning
  df$lower_text <- trimws(df$lower_text)
  df <- df[df$lower_text != "", ]
  
  # 9. Lemmatize
  df$lemma <- textstem::lemmatize_words(df$lower_text)
  
  # 10. Remove stopwords
  Stops <- as.character(Temple_stops25$word)
  df <- df[!df$lemma %in% Stops, ]
  
  # 11. Remove blank rows again after lemmatization
  df$lemma <- trimws(df$lemma)
  df <- df[df$lemma != "", ]
  
  # 12. Return clean data frame with date + lemma
  df %>% select(date, lemma)
}



TT_clean <- TrumpTweetyCleanyGenie(TrumpTweetsRaw)
```

# Loads "Lookup Database" from Github
```{r}
# Load BIG lookup database
#Your lookup database contains values or 'metadata' for many words.  I have combined many published lexical databases into a single lexical lookup database that you can use for sentiment, etc.  Let's load that in from Github and inspect it

load(url("https://github.com/Reilly-ConceptsCognitionLab/reillylab_publicdata/blob/main/lookup_Jul25.rda?raw=true"))
lookup_db <- lookup_Jul25
colnames(lookup_db)
str(lookup_db)
```

# Look up variables
```{r}
lookup_small <- lookup_db %>% select(1, 7, 25) #uses position to call arguments
str(lookup_small)
```

# Join lookup data to target text by row
```{r}
df_prep <- TT_clean %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(lookup_small, by = c("lemma" = "word")) 
print(df_prep)
```

# average sentiment per day
```{r}
df_prep$date <- TT_clean$date #left join changes the dates for some reason, but the other columns are intact, so this just replaces the changed dates with the originals


Sent_Per_Day <- df_prep %>% # average sentiment per day
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(
    AVG_arousal = mean(emo_arousal_b24_rescale, na.rm = TRUE),
    AVG_valence = mean(emo_valence_b24_rescale, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(date)
```

# get precise dates of daily polls
```{r}
PollsRaw <- PollsRaw %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date("2017-01-20") + (days - 1)
  )

Sent_Per_Day$date <- as.Date(Sent_Per_Day$date)
```

# COMBINATION
```{r}
COMBINATION <- Sent_Per_Day %>%
  full_join(PollsRaw, by = "date")

Merge <- COMBINATION %>% # correct discrepancy of trump getting kicked off twitter and end of first term
  tidyr::drop_na()

```

#granger causality
```{r}
# does valence cause polling changes
Val_cause_poll <- lmtest::grangertest(Merge$AVG_valence, Merge$Donald.Trump, order = 1)

# does arousal cause polling changes
Ar_cause_poll <- lmtest::grangertest(Merge$AVG_arousal, Merge$Donald.Trump, order = 1)

Val_cause_Ar <- lmtest::grangertest(Merge$AVG_valence, Merge$AVG_arousal, order = 1)

Val_cause_poll
Ar_cause_poll
Val_cause_Ar
```
# FML lets check correlations
```{r}
cor(Merge$Donald.Trump, Merge$AVG_arousal, use = "complete.obs")
cor(Merge$Donald.Trump, Merge$AVG_valence, use = "complete.obs")
```
# plot approval and valence correlation
```{r}
corr_value_val <- round(cor(Merge$Donald.Trump, Merge$AVG_valence, use = "complete.obs"), 3)

ggplot(Merge, aes(x = AVG_valence, y = Donald.Trump)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "blue", size = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = min(Merge$AVG_valence), 
           y = max(Merge$Donald.Trump),
           label = paste("Correlation =", corr_value_val),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 5) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Between Valence and Polling",
    x = "Average Tweet Valence",
    y = "Donald Trump Approval"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
# plot approval rating and arousal correlation
```{r}
corr_value_AR <- round(cor(Merge$Donald.Trump, Merge$AVG_arousal, use = "complete.obs"), 3)

ggplot(Merge, aes(x = AVG_arousal, y = Donald.Trump)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "blue", size = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = min(Merge$AVG_arousal), 
           y = max(Merge$Donald.Trump),
           label = paste("Correlation =", corr_value_AR),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 5) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Between Valence and Polling",
    x = "Average Tweet Arousal",
    y = "Donald Trump Approval"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
